requirement:
In authored chapters, requirements, examples, and named definitions render as
lightly framed, collapsible sections, expanded when the chapter opens. Each
header identifies the declaration and its kind. A disclosure chevron indicates
whether its body is expanded or collapsed; a subtle divider separates the
header from the expanded body. Collapsing a section hides its body while
keeping the header visible. The disclosure works with a mouse or keyboard.

The body retains its Markdown rendering, including code blocks and nested
declarations. Requirement and example headers retain the definition and
evidence links described by {cite}`requirements.index.navigation`; those
links navigate independently of the disclosure.
rationale:
The tests adequately cover each obligation in `requirements.index.declaration_sections`. **Framed, collapsible sections for all three kinds, expanded on open.** `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[declaration_sections_contain_their_headers_and_markdown_bodies]` preprocesses a chapter. The chapter has a requirement, a nested example and a named definition, plus text before and after them. The test asserts the following: - Exactly 3 `
` elements, so all three kinds are covered and each starts open. - Matching counts of `
`, `` and ``. - The sections sit between the surrounding paragraphs. **Header identifies the declaration and its kind.** - For the requirement and the example, the test checks the badge `alt="{kind} rules.{name}"` inside the header. - For the definition, it checks the `habeas-definition-label` span reading "definition" plus the escaped phrase `alpha & beta` with its anchor id. **Chevron, divider, frame and keyboard focus.** `fn[declaration_styles_distinguish_disclosure_state_and_keyboard_focus]` reads the shipped `md/habeas.css` through `stylesheet_rules`. It asserts the following: - The frame has a border and a box-shadow. - The `[open] > summary` rule has a bottom-border divider. - The `summary::before` chevron is drawn with borders and `rotate(-45deg)` when collapsed, and the `[open]` rule uses `rotate(45deg)`. - `summary:focus-visible` has an outline. - The summary has `overflow-x: auto`. Native `
`/`` supplies the mouse and keyboard disclosure, so the focus style is the only part that needs a check. `setup.rs` registers the stylesheet through `additional-css`. A separate test (`badge_stylesheet_keeps_visited_links_legible_and_shows_focus`) also checks that these selectors exist in the shipped CSS. **Collapsing hides the body and keeps the header.** The header is inside `` and the body is in a separate `habeas-declaration-body` div after it. The test asserts both facts. It checks that the header slice up to `` does not contain `habeas-declaration-body`, and that the body div follows the summary. **Markdown body retained, including code blocks and nested declarations.** The test asserts the following in the rendered HTML: - `` and `` formatting. - A `language-rust` code block. - A nested `
`. - The `:impl:` option line is stripped from the body. `fn[colon_directives_render_markdown_bodies_and_legacy_roles_stay_literal]` adds a check at the `replace_definitions` level. A body containing a `## Details` heading and a fenced code block is preserved. **Header keeps the definition and evidence links, independent of the disclosure.** For both the requirement and the example, the test asserts the header contains the `#habeas-{kind}-rules.{name}` anchor link and the `requirements-index/rules.{name}.html` evidence link. It also asserts that neither link is in the body. Both links are therefore in the summary as separate anchors. The test doesn't simulate clicks, but link navigation inside a summary is native browser behavior. The detailed link semantics belong to `requirements.index.navigation`, which is cited and is not reassessed here. No obligation lacks a test, and I found no assertion that contradicts the text. No acknowledgments apply.

text: In authored chapters, requirements, examples, and named definitions render as
lightly framed, collapsible sections, expanded when the chapter opens. Each
header identifies the declaration and its kind. A disclosure chevron indicates
whether its body is expanded or collapsed; a subtle divider separates the
header from the expanded body. Collapsing a section hides its body while
keeping the header visible. The disclosure works with a mouse or keyboard.
The body retains its Markdown rendering, including code blocks and nested
declarations. Requirement and example headers retain the definition and
links navigate independently of the disclosure.

Each requirement and example definition badge MUST link to its own anchored definition on the current page. The badge MUST have a separate adjacent link containing an accessible right-arrow icon in an integrated segment matching the badge color linking to its evidence detail page. The badge and arrow MUST remain aligned in one non-wrapping row. Definitions MUST NOT be followed by a separate plaintext evidence link. Each detail page MUST link back to the definition's anchored badge and to the index. Reference badges MUST continue to link to the definition. These links MUST resolve when a requirement name contains `.md`, as in `requirements.cli.mdbook`.
